status: frozen: wave 0 of the chart registry (plan/CHART-REGISTRY-DESIGN.md); builders start from this file

caps_notes.VIZ_MAX: charts per report (AI-chosen or engine-chosen), and items kept from plan.charts
caps_notes.VIZ_AUTO: charts the engine picks itself when no AI chart was built
caps_notes.SMALL_CELL: no printed figure rests on fewer rows: a heatmap cell is suppressed ('<5'), a bar, row or step is folded into 'other'
caps_notes.AI_CHARTS_MAX: charts in results_for_ai and in /report (the analyses' charts and the viz records together)
caps_notes.CHART_BYTES: one record's size as JSON.stringify writes it, in UTF-8 bytes (new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(record)).length). A Python producer writes a whole-number float as an integer (100, never 100.0) and measures len(json.dumps(record, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')), the same number (validate_spec.py js_bytes() checks the other float spellings). Every kind but the heatmap; a heatmap's cap is HEATMAP_BYTES. Capacity: the 10 x 12 diverging calendar of edge_heatmap_diverging is 5996 bytes, so about 120 cells fit in 6,000 bytes
caps_notes.HEATMAP_BYTES: a heatmap record's cap, measured as CHART_BYTES is (the owner's decision on the spec's byte-cap conflict, 30 Sep 2026; recorded here under the same version: the engine's nl_viz and the worker's src/charts.js already apply it; the page and the PDF draw what they receive). At 6,000 bytes about 120 cells fit, so HEAT_ROWS_MAX x HEAT_COLS_MAX (288 cells) was unreachable; at 12,000 the same calendar widened to 10 x 24 (240 cells) is 10,355 bytes, and a grid over the cap is still trimmed (pipeline.engine)
caps_notes.RECONCILE_TOL: relative tolerance of every add-up check, plus 1e-6 per part for each value's rounding to 1e-6

rules: The engine computes every value and writes every printed string (cell texts, step texts, legend lines, labels, table cells, the summary) and every tier. Renderers never format a data value: only axis ticks are formatted locally.
The AI only selects charts (plan.charts, at most 8, each with a why). The engine validates each choice against the data and builds it, or refuses it with a reason.
A chart reconciles with the engine's own overlapping figures (the menu's reconcile), or it is refused.

Privacy: no flagged column (withheld, coded, or kept by the visitor) in any role or label; no printed figure rests on fewer than SMALL_CELL (5) rows: a heatmap cell is suppressed ('<5'), a bar, row or step is folded into 'other'.
Unknown kind -> table, never dropped: a reader that does not know a record's kind, or finds its data malformed, draws its table, and a worker degrades it to kind 'table' at the same index.
Each chart renders the same on the page, in the PDF and in the share viewer, from the record alone.

grades.note: findings[].grade's words; the worker may map NOT_ENOUGH_DATA to its internal INSUFFICIENT as it does for scenario items

roles.measure: a number column the plan types flow_amount, count, level, percentage, log_scale, rating, ordinal or duration
roles.total: a number column the engine adds up: the plan types it flow_amount or count (a money or units total)
roles.units: a number column the engine adds up as units (measure.additive_kind), typed count
roles.segment: the scenarios block's segment: a column the plan types category, geography, ordinal or boolean, with 2 to 12 levels (never entity, identifier, code, free_text, metadata, date or a key role; CONTRACT-v2 5.8)
roles.category: a column the plan types category, geography, entity, ordinal or boolean (never identifier, code, free_text, metadata, date or a key role)
roles.category_or_rating: a category column, or a rating column in its own order
roles.text: a column the plan types free_text
roles.rating: a number column of 2 to 10 whole-number levels the plan types rating or ordinal

contribution_waterfall.what: each segment's contribution to the headline's change, from the prior total to the latest
conditions: the headline is a total or a row count compared over two 12-month windows (24 months of dates); never an average, a rate or a price
the category has 2 to 12 levels over the two windows, 2 or more of them with 5 or more rows in each window
the total, when named, is the headline's own measure (the scenarios basis); the category is the one the scenarios block broke the change down by
the scenarios block reconciles (basis.reconciles true)
contribution_waterfall.limit_needs: needs a total over two 12-month windows and a category of 2 to 12 levels (2 with 5 rows a window)
contribution_waterfall.source: scenarios items headline.prior, contribution.<segment>.change (the scenarios' order), headline.latest
contribution_waterfall.reconcile: the steps add up (math.fsum) to change.value and the last total equals headline.latest, to 1e-6
contribution_waterfall.privacy: the category is never a flagged column (withheld, coded or kept), never a key, identifier, code or free text, never holds a level the scrubber would change or one over 80 characters; a level with fewer than 5 rows in either window is folded into 'other'

pvm_waterfall.what: the headline's change split into price, volume and mix
conditions: the headline is a money total over two 12-month windows, and the total named is that measure
the units column is filled on every row of the claim in both windows, none negative
mix needs the category, every level of which has units in the window before; without a category the split is price and volume only
price, volume and mix add up to the change (the scenarios block's own check)
pvm_waterfall.limit_needs: needs a money total over two 12-month windows and a units column filled on every row
pvm_waterfall.reconcile: price + volume (+ mix) equals change.value to 1e-6 (math.fsum)
pvm_waterfall.privacy: as contribution_waterfall for the category; the units column is never flagged

calendar_heatmap.scale: sequential for a total (flow_amount, count, or rows when no measure is named); diverging for the month-on-month % change of a level, percentage, log_scale, rating, ordinal or duration measure
calendar_heatmap.what: month (across) by year (down) of the measure, on the engine's date column
conditions: a date column (profile.time.column) with 24 or more months over 2 or more calendar years; the latest 12 years are shown
a flow or count is totalled per month; a level, rate or index is averaged per month and shown as its % change from the month before (the month before must be above zero)
a month resting on fewer than 5 rows is suppressed; the first month and months with no rows are empty
the section is headline when the measure is the primary claim's, else other
calendar_heatmap.limit_needs: needs 24 or more months over 2 or more calendar years
calendar_heatmap.n: the month's rows; for a % change, the fewer of the two months' rows
calendar_heatmap.source: the rows the engine kept, by calendar month of the date column
calendar_heatmap.reconcile: each month's total (or average) equals the engine's own monthly series (charts trend.<claim>) where they overlap, to 1e-6
calendar_heatmap.privacy: the measure is never a flagged column; the date column is the engine's, never a withheld one

change_heatmap.what: segment (down) by month (across) of the year-on-year % change of the measure
conditions: 13 or more months of dates: a month needs the same month a year before; the latest 24 such months shown
the category has 2 to 12 levels (the 11 with the most rows and 'other')
a flow or count is totalled, a level averaged; the % change is on the same month a year before, which must be above zero
a cell needs 5 or more rows in both months; the chart is refused when fewer than half its cells can be shown
change_heatmap.limit_needs: needs half the category's level-months to hold 5 or more rows, over 13 or more months
change_heatmap.n: the fewer of the two months' rows for that level
change_heatmap.source: the rows the engine kept, by level and calendar month
change_heatmap.reconcile: each level's months add up to the engine's monthly series for the measure (all levels together), to 1e-6
change_heatmap.privacy: as contribution_waterfall for the category; the measure is never flagged

crosstab_heatmap.what: two categories against each other: rows counted, or the measure's total (a flow) or average (a level)
conditions: two different columns: the first down the side (2 to 12 levels: the 11 with the most rows and 'other'), the second across (2 to 24 levels: the 23 with the most rows and 'other'; a rating in its own order)
a cell resting on fewer than 5 rows is suppressed; the chart is refused when fewer than half its cells can be shown
crosstab_heatmap.limit_needs: needs two category columns of 2 to 24 levels
crosstab_heatmap.reconcile: the cells (suppressed ones included) add up to the rows (or the total) of the rows read, to 1e-6
crosstab_heatmap.privacy: neither column is flagged, a key, identifier, code or free text; a level the scrubber would change or over 80 characters refuses the chart; no level holds a token of a flagged column's values, and a column whose values look like people's names is refused

theme_rating_heatmap.what: the themes analysis's words (down) by rating (across): the share of each rating's texts that use the word
conditions: a free-text column the themes analysis can read (20 or more texts)
a rating column of 2 to 10 whole-number levels, in their order
rows are the themes analysis's words and phrases (at most 12, each used in 3 or more texts)
a rating with fewer than 5 texts is suppressed (n is the rating's texts); a text with no rating is counted in 'all' only
never the engine's own pick: built only when the AI plan asks for it by name
theme_rating_heatmap.limit_needs: needs a free-text column with 20 or more texts and a rating column of 2 to 10 levels
theme_rating_heatmap.source: the themes analysis's word list, counted again per rating on the same texts
theme_rating_heatmap.reconcile: each word's texts across the ratings add up to its count in the themes analysis's table
theme_rating_heatmap.privacy: never a text column that looks personal; the words are the themes analysis's, after names, emails and phone numbers are withheld; no word is a token of a flagged column's values (withheld, coded or kept), a given name (engine/first_names.txt) or a word the texts capitalise mid-sentence, and none is a word of a withheld column's name

correlation_heatmap.args_text: [measure, measure, measure, ...] (3 to 12; [] for the engine's own measures)
correlation_heatmap.what: Pearson r of each pair of measures on pairwise complete rows
conditions: 3 to 12 number columns; [] reads the engine's measures, the first 12 in its order
a pair with fewer than 5 rows holding both values is suppressed; the diagonal reads 1, tier 0
tiers use fixed cut points of |r|: below 0.3, 0.3 to 0.6, 0.6 and over
correlation_heatmap.limit_needs: needs 3 to 12 numeric columns and 10 or more rows
correlation_heatmap.source: the engine's corr chart (#9): Pearson r on pairwise complete rows
correlation_heatmap.reconcile: each r equals the corr chart's r[i][j] to 1e-6
correlation_heatmap.privacy: no flagged column, whatever the visitor decided

group_ranges.what: each group's average with its 95% bootstrap range and its median: the compare analysis as a dot plot
conditions: a measure and a category with 2 or more groups of 5 or more values (the 12 with the most rows shown)
ordered by the average weighted by rows, as the compare analysis ranks them
group_ranges.limit_needs: needs a measure and a category with 2 or more groups of 5 or more values
group_ranges.source: the compare analysis: the same seed (20260925) and 999 resamples
group_ranges.reconcile: each row's center, lo, hi and median equal the compare analysis's table to its printed digits
group_ranges.privacy: as contribution_waterfall for the category; the measure is never flagged

pareto.what: the levels ranked by their total (or rows): the top 20, the running share of the whole, and k80
conditions: a category of 8 or more levels (products, brands, stores); past the 300 values the profile lists, a column of short values the plan types category, entity or geography, up to 5,000 levels
a total that is never negative for a level (a flow or a row count); the whole above zero
the 20 largest levels with 5 or more rows are bars; every other level is in 'other' with its count; 'other' rests on 5 or more rows (the smallest bars join it until it does)
k80 counts levels in order of their totals, every level included, until they reach 80% of the whole (a count reveals no level's figure)
the engine's own pick reads only a column the plan types category, entity or geography
pareto.limit_needs: needs a category of 8 or more levels (products, brands, stores) and a total
pareto.reconcile: the bars and 'other' add up to total.value; the ranking matches the engine's ranked.<dimension> chart (#7) where they overlap
pareto.privacy: the category is never flagged, a key, identifier or code; a level under 5 rows is never a bar; no level holds a token of a flagged column's values; a column whose values look like people's names (the adapter's person-name test) is refused

slope.what: each segment's prior and latest total, joined by a line
conditions: as contribution_waterfall: the headline's total over two 12-month windows and the scenarios block's category (2 to 12 levels)
a level that entered or left has one window at 0 and change_text 'new' or 'left'
'other' rests on 5 or more rows in each window it has rows in (a both-window level with the smallest contribution joins it until it does)
slope.limit_needs: needs a total over two 12-month windows and a category of 2 to 12 levels
slope.reconcile: the a values add up to headline.prior and the b values to headline.latest, to 1e-6

waterfall.draw: one bar per step from `from` to `to`; totals in waterfall.total, a step in waterfall.rise when value > 0 else waterfall.fall; a dashed connector at each step's `to` to the next bar; the value axis always includes 0; each bar's text at its end

heatmap.draw: a grid of cells: fill by tier (colors.tier_map), the cell's text and its glyph, row and column labels from rows/cols, the axis names row_label/col_label, the legend from legend[] (swatch, glyph, text) and, when suppressed.cells > 0, suppressed.why under it

dot_range.draw: one row per group: a line from lo to hi, a dot at center, a short vertical tick at median; texts.center by the dot and 'texts.lo to texts.hi' at the right; texts.n in the row label

pareto.draw: bars largest first, then 'other' in pareto.other; the running share as a line with points on a 0-100% axis; a dashed 80% reference line; bar k80.k marked (k80) when k <= len(bars), else k80.text as the note under the chart

slope.draw: two vertical axes (a_label, b_label) on one scale; a line per row coloured by b vs a (rise, fall, flat); 'label a_text' at the left end, 'b_text change_text' at the right end, labels at each end spread at least 13 px apart with a leader line

table.draw: the record's table, captioned by the title, with the summary above it; the universal fallback: a record whose kind a reader does not know, or whose data fails its schema, is drawn as its table, never dropped

legacy.note: the analyses' own charts (series, points, fits) keep their shape and their readers; they are not viz records

schema.title: One chart record (rep.viz.charts[], results_for_ai.charts[] for a viz kind, /report charts[])

record: kind is the menu chart's draw kind (menu[chart].kind), or 'table' when a producer or reader degraded it (then degraded says from what and why)
section is the menu chart's section (calendar_heatmap: 'other' when its measure is not the primary claim's)
grade is the grade of the claim the chart shows itself; a chart derived from a graded claim has grade null and parent_grade that claim's grade; a descriptive chart has both null
every printed string is written by the engine: title, subtitle, labels, texts, legend, table cells, summary; every figure in summary is one of the record's own texts or a count stated in words
anchors are unique; 'finding:<findings[].id>', 'scenario:<scenarios.items[].id>', 'analysis:<1-based index in results_for_ai.analyses>', 'chart:<charts[].id>'
every table row has as many cells as table.cols; the table view shows every figure the chart shows
the record is at most CHART_BYTES (6000) bytes as caps_notes.CHART_BYTES measures it; a heatmap at most HEATMAP_BYTES (12000)
no string names a flagged column or holds a flagged column's value; no printed figure rests on fewer than SMALL_CELL (5) rows
waterfall: the first and the last step are the two totals (kind 'total', from 0, to = value); every step between is kind 'step'
a step's from is the previous step's to (the first step after the prior total starts at its value), and to = from + value
the steps' values add up (math.fsum) to change.value, and the last total's value equals the prior total's value + change.value, to 1e-6 x max(1, |change|, |prior|, |latest|)

at most 12 steps between the totals, in the scenarios' order: a contribution waterfall's largest |value| first, then 'other', then levels that entered or left; a price-volume-mix waterfall's price, volume, mix
heatmap: values, text, tier and n are each len(rows) x len(cols); at most 12 rows and 24 cols

a shown cell: value a finite number, text non-empty (at most 12 characters), n at least 5; the one exception: a theme_rating_heatmap's 'all' column when a rating is suppressed or 1 to 4 texts have no rating, whose value is a whole percent, its text that number and '%', and its n null (so the hidden texts cannot be worked back from it)
a suppressed cell: value null, text '<5', tier 0, n null; suppressed.cells counts them
an empty cell: value null, text '', tier 0, n 0
tier 0 with a value only on a diverging scale for a value of exactly 0, or on the correlation diagonal
sequential: tiers 0..3; diverging: a tier has the sign of its value
legend lists each tier used, lowest first; empty when no cell is shown
a month axis is 'YYYY-MM' (change_heatmap) or 'Jan'..'Dec' (calendar_heatmap); a renderer may shorten a 'YYYY-MM' label as an axis tick, never a category label
a figure too wide for 12 characters is written compact in every cell and the legend: 4 significant digits and k, M, B or T ('1.235B', '456.7M'), never refused for its width
dot_range: lo <= center <= hi for every row; n at least 5; at most 12 rows, in the compare analysis's order
pareto: bars in order of value, largest first; at most 20
cum_pct is the running sum of the bars (then 'other') over total.value x 100, non-decreasing; other.cum_pct is 100
the bars and other add up to total.value to 1e-6
k80.k is the fewest levels, in order of their totals, every level included, that reach 80% of the whole (so it always exists); k80.of counts every level: len(bars) + other.n_entities
slope: at most 12 rows; a and b are the two windows' totals; change_text the level's own change, or 'new' / 'left'
table: data is {}; the chart is its table: table.cols is not empty

tiers.sequential: tertiles of the shown values: q1 and q2 are the 1/3 and 2/3 percentiles (numpy 'linear'); tier 1 when value <= q1, 2 when <= q2, else 3
tiers.diverging: tertiles of |value| over the shown non-zero cells (one scale for both signs); tier = sign(value) x (1 when |value| <= q1, 2 when <= q2, else 3); a value of exactly 0 is tier 0
tiers.correlation: fixed cut points of |r|: tier +/-1 below 0.3, +/-2 from 0.3 to below 0.6, +/-3 from 0.6; the diagonal is tier 0
tiers.legend: each tier's text names its range with the cell texts' own formatter: 'lo to q1', 'q1 to q2', 'q2 to hi'; diverging, each side to its own extreme: falls '-maxfall to -q2', '-q2 to -q1', '-q1 to 0%', rises '0% to q1', 'q1 to q2', 'q2 to maxrise' (a bound past a side's extreme is that extreme)
tiers.glyph_rule: by |tier|: ○ (1), ◐ (2), ● (3), after the cell's text, in cell_text colour; tier 0 has none. The page prints the characters (aria-hidden: the text carries the value); the PDF draws them as vectors (WinAnsi has no such glyphs): a circle of radius 2.4 pt, stroke 0.7 pt; tier 1 the outline, tier 2 the outline with its left half filled, tier 3 filled

colors.from: portfolio-website/build.py: TOKENS and heat_tokens() (the site's contrast-checked build tokens). The design's light hexes are these tokens; the dark ones are the same tokens' dark values. suppressed.fill is new: mix(surface, muted, 0.10), the build's own mix().

tier_map.diverging: tier -k fills falls[k]; tier +k fills rises[k] (k = 1..3)
tier_map.zero: tier 0 is no fill: empty (value null, text ''), suppressed (text '<5'), or neutral (a value of exactly 0 on a diverging scale, the correlation diagonal)

colors.pdf: the PDF uses the light palette only

accessibility.accessible_name: title + '. ' + summary: the page's figure and svg carry it (role='img', aria-label); the share viewer the same; the PDF prints the title as the figure caption and the summary under it
accessibility.table_view: every chart has its table view (record.table): on the page and in the share viewer a 'Show as table' control under the chart, open by default for kind 'table'; the table's <caption> is the title; in the PDF the table follows the chart when it has at most 12 rows, else it goes to the appendix and the caption says so
not_colour_alone: a number in every heatmap cell, and a ○◐● glyph for its tier
a + or − sign on every change (the engine's texts)
waterfall totals are labelled; a rise and a fall differ by sign, not only by colour
a suppressed cell reads '<5' and has a dashed border; an empty one is blank with a dashed border
the pareto's k80 bar is marked with text; a slope's direction is in its change_text
accessibility.contrast: text at least 4.5:1 on its fill, marks at least 3:1 on the surface, in both themes (colors.contrast holds the measured minimums)
accessibility.keyboard: each chart is focusable (tabindex 0) with its accessible name; no figure is shown only in a tooltip
accessibility.motion: no animation is needed; any transition honours prefers-reduced-motion
accessibility.language: labels keep their script; right-to-left labels (Arabic, Hebrew) are set with dir='auto'

rules: no chart or label makes the page wider than the viewport; only a table view scrolls sideways, inside its own box (overflow-x: auto) with its first column sticky and an edge fade as the cue
text at least 11 px on the page (7 pt in the PDF); rows at least 24 px; tap targets at least 24 px
a label is never reworded: one that does not fit is clipped with an ellipsis at a character boundary and shown whole in the tooltip and the table view
axis ticks are the only numbers a renderer formats (3 to 5 ticks, the locale's grouping)

waterfall.wide: vertical bars when every bar gets at least 44 px, labels under the bars
waterfall.narrow: horizontal: one row per step, the label on its own line above its bar (full width), the bar below it with its text at its end; totals bold; 14 steps fit in 34 px rows

heatmap.cell_px: a cell needs max(30, 6.6 x its longest text + 22) px: the number and its glyph
heatmap.wide: columns across when every cell fits
heatmap.narrow: transposed when that fits; else the column axis is split into blocks of as many columns as fit, stacked, each block repeating the row labels (a 10-year calendar at 288 px: months down, 3 years a block); cells never shrink below their need

dot_range.wide: label left, the line to its right, texts at the right
dot_range.narrow: the label above its line, texts.center by the dot and 'lo to hi' under the line

pareto.wide: vertical bars with the running-share line on a right-hand 0-100% axis
pareto.narrow: horizontal bars, the label above each; cum_text in its own right-hand column; the 80% reference is a divider row after bar k80 (or k80.text as the note)

slope.wide: two axes, when both ends' labels fit (360 px and up)
slope.narrow: a dumbbell list: one row per label (label above), a dot at a and at b on one shared axis, an arrow from a to b, a_text and b_text under the dots, change_text at the right

table.all: its own scroller; first column sticky

phone_fit.pdf: the PDF draws the wide layout within its text column (475 pt on A4, 492 pt on Letter) and the narrow one when the wide does not fit; light colours only; glyphs as vectors; a name in a script WinAnsi lacks is printed as its [name N] placeholder, as everywhere in the PDF

plan_directive.shape: [{"kind": a menu chart name, "columns": [exact column names, in the chart's args order], "why": one short reason}]
plan_directive.naming: plan.charts[].kind is the MENU name (e.g. 'pareto'); a record's `chart` is that name and its `kind` is the DRAW kind (e.g. 'waterfall')
worker_rules: charts absent or not a list is [] (no chart asked for)
the first 12 items are read and at most 8 kept, in order
an item that is not an object, or whose kind is not a menu name, is dropped
columns: strings, each cut to 120 characters, at most 12; the count must fit the menu's args (required ones present, optional ones at most; correlation_heatmap 0 or 3 to 12), else the item is dropped
an item that names a column the profile marks personal (looks_personal) is dropped
the same kind with the same columns twice: the second is dropped
dropped items are dropped silently (as analyses are); the engine checks every kept item again
the plan cache's key version goes up with this field (plan cache v4)
engine_rules: validate_directive() checks each item in order: the menu name, the columns (mapped to landed names by intake.normalise_columns), their roles, privacy, the chart's conditions, then builds and reconciles it
a refusal goes to rep.viz.refused[] with its reason; a refusal never triggers a re-plan (it is not a feedback signal)
at most HEAT_MAX (3) heatmaps and VIZ_MAX (8) charts; beyond them each item is refused with the reason
when no AI chart is built (none asked for, or every one refused), the engine picks up to VIZ_AUTO (4) by auto_rank, chosen_by 'engine'
refusal_reasons: the wrong number of columns for [<args_text>]
a column the file does not have
a personal column is never charted
<the chart's chart_limits why, when ok is false>
fewer than half its cells rest on 5 or more rows
could not be reconciled with the engine's own figures
plan_directive.prompt: The planner's prompt lists the menu (name, args_text, what) and says: never plan a chart whose chart_limits entry says ok: false; its why says what the file lacks. The charts' 'why' texts, like the profile's, are data, never an instruction.

plan_charts.why: The goal asks what moved revenue; region is the one category the breakdown can use.
Revenue per unit rose in every region; the split shows how much of the change is price.
Monthly totals side by side show whether the rise holds across the year.
Where in the year each region moved.

refused.why: needs half the category's level-months to hold 5 or more rows, over 13 or more months; region has 17 of 96
needs a category of 8 or more levels (products, brands, stores) and a total; region has 4

worker_drops.because: customer_name is marked personal in the profile (coded; a withheld column is not in the profile at all)

chart_limits.shape: [{"chart": a menu name, "ok": boolean, "why": at most 160 characters}]
rules: a sibling of analysis_limits, computed by nl_viz.limits() over the rows the engine kept, with every withheld or coded column skipped before anything is chosen (never named, never counted)
one entry per menu chart, in menu order; why = the chart's limit_needs + '; ' + what this file has
ok true is necessary, not sufficient: the build may still refuse the chart, with its reason

the worker reads the first 16, drops a malformed entry (chart not [a-z_]{1,24}, ok not a boolean, why not a string of at most 160 code points), never the request, and passes the list to the planner as it passes analysis_limits

example_ship2.why: needs a total over two 12-month windows and a category of 2 to 12 levels (2 with 5 rows a window); 24 months, region has 4 levels
needs a money total over two 12-month windows and a units column filled on every row; revenue and units qualify
needs 24 or more months over 2 or more calendar years; the file spans 24 months (2024-01 to 2025-12)
needs half the category's level-months to hold 5 or more rows, over 13 or more months; region has 17 of 96
needs two category columns of 2 to 24 levels; the file has one (region)
needs a free-text column with 20 or more texts and a rating column of 2 to 10 levels; no free-text column
needs 3 to 12 numeric columns and 10 or more rows; the file has 2 (revenue, units)
needs a measure and a category with 2 or more groups of 5 or more values; region has 4 such groups
needs a category of 8 or more levels (products, brands, stores) and a total; region has 4
needs a total over two 12-month windows and a category of 2 to 12 levels; region has 4 levels

auto_rank.when: no AI chart was built (none asked for, or every one refused)

base.note: 0-9 by plan.kind (a plan without a kind reads 'other'); never theme_rating_heatmap, and a pareto only on a column the plan types category, entity or geography

bonus.primary: +3 when the chart's total or measure is the plan's primary column
bonus.analysis: +2 when the plan ran the matching analysis: compare -> group_ranges, themes -> theme_rating_heatmap, relationship -> correlation_heatmap, rank or share -> pareto, trend or extremes -> calendar_heatmap
bonus.goal: +1 for each goal keyword the plan's goal contains (at most +2)

auto_rank.pick: only charts whose limit is ok and that build; highest score first, ties in menu order; at most VIZ_AUTO (4) and at most HEAT_MAX (3) heatmaps; why = 'Chosen by the engine: <what>' (at most 200 characters)

engine: engine/nl_viz.py: REGISTRY (the menu), build(rep, ctx), limits(), validate_directive(), cards_for_ai(), v2_records(); constants from caps
rep['viz'] = {version, charts: [records], refused: [{chart, columns, why, chosen_by}], chosen_by: 'ai'|'engine'|'none'}; blank_report carries {version, charts: [], refused: [], chosen_by: 'none'}

build() runs after rep['scenarios']; each record is appended to rep['charts'] as a v2 record: {id, rule: 'V', type: 'viz', title, view: 'manager', default_visible: true, finding_ids (the anchors' finding ids), why_shown: why, source, data: the record}; rule V records are drawn in the page's viz area and are not counted in section 3's six manager records

results_for_ai.charts: the analyses' charts first (their order), then the viz records, at most AI_CHARTS_MAX (10) in all; every string through the same safe(); a viz record is sent whole (data included: the share viewer and the PDF draw from it)
the byte budget: after the scenario items, viz records go from the end before any analysis does

a record over its byte cap (HEATMAP_BYTES for a heatmap, CHART_BYTES for every other kind) is trimmed before it is emitted, one step at a time until it fits: a calendar_heatmap drops its oldest year, a change_heatmap its oldest month, a crosstab folds its last row into 'other', a theme x rating heatmap drops its last word, a correlation heatmap its last measure, a pareto folds its last bar into 'other' (a waterfall, a dot range and a slope always fit); tiers, legend and summary are computed on what is kept, and the subtitle ends with what is shown ('2018 to 2026 shown: the chart's size limit'); a record that cannot be trimmed to fit is refused ('too large to draw')
worker: src/charts.js sanitizeChart(record): every field cut to the schema's caps; kind at most 10 characters; a kind this worker does not know, data that fail their kind's schema or invariants, or a record over its byte cap (HEATMAP_BYTES for a heatmap, CHART_BYTES otherwise) is degraded to kind 'table' (data {}, degraded {from, why}); a table over CHART_BYTES loses rows from the end; a chart is never removed, so [CHART:n] keeps its meaning
defence in depth: a heatmap cell with a value and n under 5 is suppressed ('<5', tier 0, value and n null) and counted in suppressed.cells; a dot_range row with n under 5 is removed and counted
legacy kinds (line, bars, scatter) keep today's sanitising

report.js keeps at most AI_CHARTS_MAX (10) charts; the model gets a card per viz chart, never its data: {n, kind, title, section, supports, grade, parent_grade, summary, table}; only a card's summary and table are indexed by the guard

G10: a [CHART:n] marker for a viz chart outside its section ('the headline', 'what drove it', 'other findings', 'scenarios') is moved into that section; a section the report lacks leaves it where it is
/report returns the validated charts and tables it used; the page and the share viewer draw those, never their own copy
share.js stores the same validated charts (the share's caps apply by whole records, from the end)
page: src/js/55-nl-viz.js draws the five kinds and the table fallback from the record alone
N.check (52-nl2-report.js) accepts type 'viz' through SHAPE.viz (the record schema); an unknown kind is drawn as its table, never a reason to fall back to the v1 report
50-try.js resolves [CHART:n] and builds shares from /report's returned charts
rep.viz.refused is listed under the charts in the analyst view, in the engine's words (the chart's name in the reader's words, and why)
pdf: a VIZ dispatch on kind: waterfall, heatmap, dot_range, pareto, slope; 'table' and any unknown kind as the table; legacy kinds unchanged
